blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Uncertainty quantification for novel view synthesis with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) assesses rendering reliability at unseen viewpoints. This reliability depends on the discrepancy between rendered and true colors, which cannot be measured without ground-truth images. We therefore quantify uncertainty in this unknown discrepancy through upper bounds on per-pixel RGB mean absolute error. However, learned bounds may underestimate these errors and overstate rendering reliability, motivating calibration to a prescribed coverage level. In this paper, we propose QuantileGS, a post-hoc framework that combines learned rendering-error quantiles with scale-normalized conformal calibration to produce spatially adaptive error bounds. The framework comprises three phases. Phase 1, Rendering-Error Computation, measures RGB mean absolute error between observed images and predictions from a frozen 3DGS model. Phase 2, Ordered Gaussian Quantile Fields, learns two scalar attributes per Gaussian to predict lower and upper rendering-error quantiles. Phase 3, Scale-Normalized Conformal Calibration, calibrates the upper prediction on held-out images, using the quantile gap to scale the correction. Under the stated assumptions, the resulting bounds provide finite-sample marginal coverage. At a nominal coverage level of 90%, calibration raises mean empirical test coverage from 69.6% to 89.6% on LLFF and from 80.1% to 92.1% on Mip-NeRF 360. On LF, coverage remains conservative at 96.3% before and 96.4% after calibration. Applications to active view selection, Gaussian pruning, and RGB-D simultaneous localization and mapping illustrate how these bounds inform downstream decisions.

blocks.en:
Uncertainty quantification (UQ) for novel view synthesis (NVS) with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) [ 25 , 7 ] assesses the reliability of images rendered from previously unseen viewpoints. Despite advances in generative view synthesis [ 10 ] , efficient rendering [ 46 ] , and sparse-view
reconstruction [ 52 , 51 , 49 ] ,
high reconstruction quality on observed views does not ensure accurate predictions at unseen viewpoints. Occlusion, limited observations, and view-dependent appearance leave scene properties weakly constrained, producing errors that vary across pixels and viewpoints. The reliability of a rendered pixel depends on its agreement with the ground-truth RGB at the requested viewpoint, which is unavailable at inference. We therefore characterize the predictive uncertainty of a fixed 3DGS model through the RGB errors its predictions may incur. Specifically, we estimate upper quantiles of per-pixel RGB mean absolute error (RGB-MAE), the average absolute discrepancy across the three color channels. This expresses uncertainty in terms of how large the unknown rendering error may be.

blocks.en:
Existing methods estimate rendering uncertainty through parameter
variation [ 28 , 30 , 40 , 22 ] , rendering sensitivity [ 23 ] , and cross-view
consistency [ 34 ] . Others use reconstruction residuals and observation coverage to predict errors or identify unreliable
regions [ 14 , 17 , 29 ] .
These approaches characterize different aspects of rendering reliability.
Prediction variability and rendering sensitivity describe how outputs change, but do not by themselves measure agreement with ground truth. For example, predictions from different model samples can agree closely while sharing a systematic color bias. Learning from reconstruction residuals connects uncertainty more directly to observed RGB discrepancies, providing a basis for interpreting the reliability of a fixed renderer in terms of its prediction errors.

To this end, we propose QuantileGS, a post-hoc framework that estimates and calibrates rendering-error uncertainty with a frozen pretrained 3DGS model.
Two nonnegative attributes per Gaussian parameterize ordered lower and upper RGB-MAE quantile fields. Shared across views, these attributes yield view-dependent
predictions through the original α \alpha -blending weights and fixed background values. Conformal calibration adjusts the upper prediction using the
floored interquantile gap as a local scale [ 33 , 5 ] .
Calibration and test views are excluded from RGB pretraining and quantile fitting. Novel-view bounds require camera parameters but no target RGB.
Under exchangeability of pixel-level calibration and test scores, conditional on fitting, the bounds provide finite-sample marginal
coverage [ 26 ] . This guarantee averages over the calibration sample and a new pixel observation, without implying a separate coverage guarantee for each view or pixel location.

empirical coverage, and mean upper bounds. Prior work uses uncertainty for diffusion-based scene refinement [ 9 ] , active view selection

blocks.en: 4.5 Downstream Applications
blocks.zh: 4.5 下游应用

blocks.en:
We use calibrated RGB-MAE bounds u ⁡ ( 𝒙 ) u(\bm{x}) to guide three downstream applications. For active view selection , the bounds weight the
reduction of a local prediction-variance proxy, favoring views informative about regions with larger bounds. For Gaussian pruning , they combine with estimated
deletion perturbations to assess deletion costs while accounting for unknown rendering residuals. For RGB-D SLAM , they limit reference-color corrections

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We presented QuantileGS, a post-hoc UQ framework that learns ordered error quantiles for a frozen 3DGS renderer. Scale-normalized conformal calibration yields spatially
adaptive RGB-MAE upper bounds with finite-sample marginal coverage under the stated assumptions. Experiments on LF, LLFF, and Mip-NeRF 360 show improved error
ranking over the evaluated baselines. Calibration reduces empirical undercoverage on LLFF and Mip-NeRF 360, while LF bounds remain conservative. Applications to active view selection, Gaussian pruning, and RGB-D SLAM empirically demonstrate the downstream
utility of the calibrated bounds.

根据所述假设,适应性RGB-MAE上限,有有限样本的边际覆盖。 关于LF、LLFF和Mip-NERF360的实验显示有改进错误
在评估基线上排名。 校准减少了LLFF和Mip-NERF 360上的经验性卧底,而LF界限仍然保守. 用于活动视图选择的应用程序 Gaussian pruning 和 RGB-D SLAM 实证演示下游
校准界限的实用性。

blocks.en:
AVS selects camera viewpoints to improve scene reconstruction under a limited acquisition budget.
Building on the local information approximation of FisherRF [ 23 ] , we prioritize views that supply missing information about parameters affecting regions with large calibrated error bounds.

blocks.en:
We adopt the alternating tracking-mapping organization of Gaussian-SLAM [ 48 ] .
Gaussian-SLAM estimates poses against a rendered Gaussian submap, while VarSplat [ 37 ] additionally uses learned appearance variance to weight photometric residuals.
Our integration uses QuantileGS to construct reference images with calibrated rendering-error bounds.
New frames are aligned with these cached RGB-D references by reprojection, and their bounds determine the robust scales of the photometric tracking loss.
Thus, Gaussian rendering supplies the reference appearance, while pose optimization operates on image correspondences.

We study the effect of calibration on all nine Mip-NeRF 360
scenes using the original RGB checkpoints and quantile fields from our pruning protocol, evaluated before any pruning or recovery.
The RGB renderer and the learned quantile fields remain fixed throughout this analysis.
In particular, the fitted quantile levels are η = 0.5 \eta=0.5 and τ = 0.9 \tau=0.9 for every variant, and changing the calibration target does not involve refitting these fields. We reuse the saved fitting, calibration, and test partitions, with 21-54 calibration views per scene, and use seed 0. No test observations are used to determine the calibration corrections.
